sampling_model.design: The headline theorems use balanced complete randomization, uniform over assignments with exactly \(n=N/K\) units in each arm. The open kernel problem ranges only over laws in \(\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\): every realized allocation has those fixed counts and every unit has marginal arm probability \(1/K\), without exchangeability.
sampling_model.units: The \(N\) units and all \(K\) potential outcomes per unit are fixed; there is no super-population sampling.
sampling_model.treatment: The assignment vector \(Z\) is the sole random object and is generated by the known complete-randomization law or the known admissible nonexchangeable law \(p\).
sampling_model.overlap: Each arm has known marginal assignment probability \(1/K\) and a positive fixed allocation count.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The identification theorem conditions on the armwise empirical marginal laws \(F\); empirical estimation of those margins is outside the first structural kernel and follows the quantile plug-in route of Aronow, Green, and Lee.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The upper bound is attained if the two potential outcomes are comonotonic.
An integer program computes a worst-case copula for broad designs and estimators.
Multi-marginal optimal transport gives exact identified sets for general quadratic cross-world objectives.
The design-based framework permits arbitrary multi-arm contrast matrices.
Supermodular expectations are monotone in concordance for distributions with fixed marginals.
The identity permutation is optimal for a Robinson similarity and dissimilarity when one is Toeplitz.
Isotone imputation converges to a least-favourable two-arm limiting experiment.

body.tldr: Under balanced complete randomization, the common-rank potential-outcome completion is universally least favourable for the scalarized covariance loss \(\operatorname{tr}\{W\operatorname{Cov}_Z(C\widehat{\bar Y})\}\) if and only if the contrast Gram matrix \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\) is a graph Laplacian. This gives an \(O(K^2)\) certificate, exact six-unit audit examples, and a binary counterexample outside the cone. Common ranks dominate the entire multi-contrast covariance matrix only for a vector-rescaled pairwise contrast. For a general admissible balanced covariance tensor, cut expansion gives an exact finite copositivity characterization and, for exact real-algebraic inputs, an exhaustive root-isolation and linear-feasibility algorithm. Polynomial-time recognition and the minimal complete failure-witness alphabet remain open.

project_justification.gap: Sharp rank completion is analytic for the two-arm difference-in-means estimator, whereas generalized causal-bootstrap work uses integer programming for broad designs and estimators. The literature does not state the exact contrast-geometry boundary at which one common-rank completion remains universally least favourable in a multi-arm experiment. On the realizable nonexchangeable balanced-kernel domain, the remaining gap is a polynomial-time recognition method, or a faithful hardness result, together with a minimal-alphabet separating certificate.
project_justification.niche: The object is neither a generic transport solver nor another conservative covariance estimator. It is a design-computable graph-Laplacian cone for complete randomization, a sharper classification for joint covariance dominance, and an exact cut-copositivity representation on the admissible balanced moment polytope modulo common unit relabelling.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the complete-randomization risk decomposition, proves the graph-Laplacian equivalence by finite rearrangement and isolated binary necessity witnesses, evaluates both mechanisms exactly at \(K=3,N=6\), and classifies the Loewner case. For general balanced kernels it proves that identity-optimality is equivalent to copositivity of finitely many explicit cut matrices and supplies a terminating exact algebraic algorithm with multilevel witnesses, while leaving polynomial complexity and the minimal complete alphabet as explicit residual questions.

body.related_work: Aronow, Green, and Lee establish the two-arm comonotone sharp endpoint, which the two-arm proposition recovers exactly. Imbens and Menzel use the same isotone completion to obtain a least-favourable limiting experiment. Zhao and Ding supply the arbitrary-contrast complete-randomization covariance identity but do not optimize its unidentified cross-arm terms. Tchen's supermodular-order theorem is consistent with the pairwise rearrangement mechanism, while the proof here gives the needed finite permutation argument directly. Gao, Ge, and Qian formulate general quadratic cross-world extrema as multi-marginal transport, and Brennan et al. compute generalized causal-bootstrap completions by integer programming. The present general-kernel theorem instead restricts to covariance tensors in the exact finite moment-polytope image of balanced assignment laws and gives a finite cut-copositivity characterization. Laurent and Seminaroti's Robinson--Toeplitz result concerns a sufficient identity-optimal class for a two-matrix quadratic assignment problem; it does not supply the necessary-and-sufficient or polynomial recognition result sought here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The graph-Laplacian certificate concerns a prespecified scalar covariance loss \(W\) and does not turn that endpoint into a sharp matrix-valued covariance bound. Except for a rescaled pairwise contrast, no single common-rank completion dominates every linear combination simultaneously. For general balanced kernels, the copositivity theorem is an exhaustive finite characterization: it enumerates factorially many relabellings and arm permutations and exponentially many supports, and its strict witnesses may have as many as \(N\) ordered levels per arm. It therefore does not satisfy the open polynomial-time or binary-certificate requirement.
body.honest_scope: The complete-randomization cone theorem follows from the design covariance identity plus a finite rearrangement proof and a new contrast-geometry necessity classification; novelty lies in the causal contrast cone and Loewner boundary, not in a new general dependence inequality. The six-unit propositions are audit certificates rather than asymptotic claims. The general balanced-kernel contribution is presently the exact cut-copositivity equivalence and a terminating algorithm only for exact real-algebraic inputs. No algebraic enumeration is claimed for unrestricted real inputs, and no polynomial runtime, hardness classification, binary completeness, or minimal-alphabet theorem is claimed.
body.interpretation: For complete randomization, a practitioner needs only inspect the off-diagonal signs of \(C^{\mathsf T}WC\): nonpositive signs certify one-sort least-favourable completion, while any positive sign identifies two arms on which a binary reversal strictly improves the loss. Matrix-valued conservativeness is much rarer and occurs only for a rescaled single pairwise contrast. Under a nonexchangeable balanced design, the analogous exact question is a finite family of copositivity tests after choosing a common unit order; this is mathematically decidable for exact algebraic inputs but is not yet a scalable certificate.
